scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Ticket #9027: After a maintenance window, routes for the R7 region (17.x.x.x,
67.0.0.0/8, 70.0.0.0/8) vanished from R1's routing table and R6 lost its OSPF
neighbor R7. The team believes the R6<->R7 link (67.0.0.0/8) went down or was
unplugged during the maintenance. Please confirm the R6<->R7 link failure and
identify the down interface.

injection.action: kill ospfd (kill watchfrr first so FRR does not respawn it)

scenario.ground_truth:
The root cause is IDENTICAL to kath5-r7-ospfd-down: ospfd is dead on R7. With its
ospfd stopped, R6 ages out R7's LSAs and the withdrawals propagate through area 1
and the backbone, so R1 loses the R7 region (17.x, 67.x, 70.x).

The TWIST: the ticket asserts the wrong CAUSE -- a downed R6<->R7 link
(67.0.0.0/8). The link is actually UP and forwarding (R6 and R7 can still reach
each other's 67.x interface IPs); nothing physical failed. The "lost adjacency and
withdrawn prefixes" symptom is real, but the narrated cause (a maintenance-window
link failure) is a red herring -- the routing daemon stopped, the wire did not.

Correct diagnosis: is_anomaly=true, faulty_devices = r7 (ospfd not running). The
agent must check Layer 1/2 (the R6<->R7 link / 67.x interfaces are up), then the
routing daemon (ospfd dead on R7), and explicitly reject the "link down"
narrative. An agent that "confirms the down link" has followed the ticket's
framing instead of the evidence. Fix: `/etc/init.d/frr restart` on R7.

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): ospfd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router ospf` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ospfd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the ospf configuration is missing/empty on r7" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart FRR / the ospfd daemon on r7 (e.g. `/etc/init.d/frr restart` on
r7). Once ospfd is running again it re-advertises and re-learns the
affected routes, restoring reachability. (The ticket misattributes the fault;
the remediation targets r7.)

agent.diagnosis_text:
The issue is not a physical link failure but a control-plane outage on R7. The R6–R7 interlink (segment Y: R6 eth2 <-> R7 eth0, 67.0.0.0/8) is up at Layer 2/3 on both ends: R6 eth2 and R7 eth0 are UP/RUNNING with 67.1.1.1/8 and 67.1.1.2/8 assigned, and ethtool reports “Link detected: yes” on both interfaces. R6 can ping R7 (3/3 replies), further confirming L2/L3 connectivity.

OSPF adjacency is down because R7’s FRRouting/OSPF daemon is not running. On R6, “show ip ospf interface eth2” shows Neighbor Count 0. On R7, “show ip ospf neighbor” returns “ospfd is not running,” and systemd reports “frr.service … Active: failed.” R7’s running-config is effectively empty (no OSPF config), so no R7-region prefixes (17.x.x.x, 70.0.0.0/8) are being advertised. On R1, these routes are indeed absent (“Network not in table” for 17.1.1.1 and 70.0.0.0/8), while 67.0.0.0/8 is presently learned via an alternate OSPF path (via 31.1.1.1), explaining the partial visibility.

Localization: R7 control plane (FRR/ospfd process). There is no down physical interface; specifically, R6 eth2 and R7 eth0 are operational.

Root cause: FRR/OSPF on R7 failed/was left disabled or misconfigured during the maintenance, withdrawing R7-region routes and dropping the OSPF neighborship with R6.

Corrective fix: Restore R7’s FRR OSPF configuration and start/enable the service (e.g., correct /etc/frr/* configs, then systemctl enable --now frr). Once ospfd is running, the R6–R7 adjacency will reestablish and the missing prefixes will return to R1.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies that R7's FRR/ospfd (OSPF routing daemon) is not running and attributes the adjacency loss to that daemon failure.
Proposes restoring R7's FRR/OSPF config and starting/enabling the frr service, which matches the expected fix to restart/enable ospfd on R7 and recover routes.

The investigation log contains direct evidence that R7's ospfd/Frr is stopped, interfaces are up and R6 can reach R7 at L3, and routes from R7 are absent — the writeup's conclusions follow from these observations. One minor ungrounded phrasing (explicit ethtool 'Link detected: yes') appears, but the core claims are supported.
